Result: A recent minor crash put our drone out of service for seven days, delaying two village orthophoto deliveries and raising local partners' concerns about scheduling reliability.

Can we schedule a 30‑min call to review the parts list and insurance terms?

Regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer

Subject: Request for Spare Parts and Insurance to Ensure Mapping Operations Continuity

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I am writing to report a recent minor drone crash that resulted in the drone being out of service for seven days. Unfortunately, this downtime has delayed two village orthophoto deliveries, which has raised concerns among our local partners regarding our scheduling reliability.

To mitigate the risk of similar incidents and ensure continuity of our mapping operations during field campaigns, I am requesting €2,600 to procure the following spare parts and services:

- Spare propellers and motors
- Two additional batteries
- One spare gimbal
- One-year basic insurance

The purpose of these purchases is to reduce downtime risk and minimize disruptions to our field campaigns. By having these essential components in stock, we can quickly replace damaged parts and continue our mapping operations without delays.

I would like to schedule a 30-minute call to review the parts list and insurance terms in more detail. Please let me know a convenient time for you, and I will make sure to adjust my schedule accordingly.

If approved, I will proceed with the procurement of the required items as soon as possible.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,

Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer

Topology errors are quite common and can be easily checked. To do this, I recommend reprojecting your raster to EPSG:3857 only for web display purposes. Best regards,
[Your Name]

If you want, I can provide a set of photo-to-log comparisons.
Please advise next steps.

task_instruction: Give compact instructions to use Sentinel-2 data for vegetation change detection.

personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Download Sentinel-2 L2A from Copernicus (https://scihub.copernicus.eu) for two dates > load band 8 (NIR) and band 4 (red). Compute NDVI for each: (B8 - B4)/(B8 + B4) and save ndvi_2019.tif, ndvi_2024.tif. Use Raster Calculator: ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 > save as ndvi_change.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping and align/resample rasters to same grid (use gdalwarp -tr 10 10). Mask small changes <0.05 to remove noise. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check cloud cover and recommend dates to use.
prompt:
Write a email

- Task: process two Sentinel-2 L2A scenes (one from 2019 and one from 2024).
- Data source: Copernicus SciHub (https://scihub.copernicus.eu).
- Bands to use: Band 8 (NIR) and Band 4 (red).
- NDVI calculation: NDVI = (B8 - B4) / (B8 + B4).
- Output files for NDVI: ndvi_2019.tif and ndvi_2024.tif.
- Change detection: use Raster Calculator to compute ndvi_change = ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 and save as ndvi_change.tif.
- Preprocessing requirement: check projection before clipping; align/resample rasters to the same grid.
- Recommended command for resampling/alignment: gdalwarp -tr 10 10.
- Noise filtering: mask out small changes with absolute value < 0.05.
- Offer: sender can review the project file if recipient wants.
- Sender action: sender will check cloud cover and recommend which dates to use.

personalized:
Quick note: Print Layout scale bar shows incorrect ground distances after reprojecting project CRS.
Environment: QGIS 3.8.0, Windows 10, project initially EPSG:4326 then changed to EPSG:32634. Attached: scalebar_bug.qgz.
Steps to reproduce: open scalebar_bug.qgz > Project CRS EPSG:4326 > open Layout 'Main' > note scale bar reading for map at 1:5000 > change Project CRS to EPSG:32634 > refresh Layout.
Observed behaviour: Scale bar now reads 1:10000 while map scale remains 1:5000; measured distances on map disagree with scale bar labels.
stacktrace: QgisMessageLog: 2025-05-02T09:30:12Z "Composer: ScaleBar::updateUnits: Projection conversion error: 'Cannot compute ground distance'
Expected behaviour vs actual behaviour: Scale bar should update and represent accurate ground distances after project CRS change. Actual: labels and units wrong.
Workaround: Manually set scale in layout to match, but this is not reliable for templates.
Please advise and provide an estimated timeline for a fix or a documented procedure to ensure correct scale bar behaviour after reprojection.
Regards,
Marko Petrović

Subject: Proposal for Standardized Photo Naming Convention and Data Collection Protocol

Dear Team,

I am writing to address the current issue of slow photo linking to features due to varying file names. To streamline this process and improve data management, I propose adopting a standardized photo naming convention, along with additional requirements for capturing and recording metadata.

The proposed photo naming convention is in the format: selo_featureID_timestamp, where:

-'selo' is a prefix to identify the dataset
- 'featureID' is the unique identifier for the feature
- 'timestamp' is the date and time the photo was taken (in the format 'YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ')

Example: DonjiBrijeg_BLDG_012_20260104T0930Z

To further enhance data collection, I recommend the following requirements:

1. When photographing features, please capture the compass bearing of the camera.
2. Ensure that GPS coordinates are embedded in the photo EXIF metadata.
3. Populate a 'photo_ref' field in the data collection form, linking the photo to the corresponding feature.

With this standardized naming convention, compass bearing, and GPS coordinates embedded in EXIF metadata, and a 'photo_ref' field, photos can be automatically joined to feature attributes
